title: Give a Shopping Job Before You Enter | Parenting Rewind
audience_intent: Adults and parents; not directed to children
education_scope: General parenting education only; not personalised therapy, diagnosis, or medical advice.

narration.transcript: A busy supermarket asks a five-year-old to wait, follow, ignore bright displays, and remember rules all at once. Giving directions only after grabbing begins can leave the child without a clear role during the hardest moments. Pause before entering and offer one concrete, age-appropriate job. Try: Stay beside the trolley and find three red apples for our bag; when that is done, I will give you the next job. A specific job gives attention somewhere useful while one-step directions remain easier to understand and praise.

source.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
source.title: Tips for Giving Directions
